clusters.name: Obsessions (DSM p.265, Dulcan p.366)
items: Intrusive unwanted thoughts, urges, or images causing anxiety/distress (DSM p.265)
Attempts to ignore, suppress, or neutralize with another thought or action (DSM p.265)

clusters.name: Compulsions (DSM p.265, Dulcan p.366)
items: Repetitive behaviors or mental acts in response to obsession or rigid rules (DSM p.265)
Aimed at reducing distress/preventing dreaded event, but excessive or unrealistic (DSM p.265)

criteria.thresholds: Time-consuming (>1 hour/day) or clinically significant distress/impairment (DSM p.265, Dulcan p.366)

epidemiology.prevalence: 1-2% in children (Dulcan p.368); 2-3% adult lifetime (DSM p.267, Synopsis ch.9)
epidemiology.sex_ratio: Male preponderance in childhood (Dulcan p.368, DSM p.268); 1:1 in adulthood (DSM p.268)
epidemiology.onset_age_typical: Mean 9-10 years in children (Dulcan p.367-368); bimodal peaks (childhood and young adulthood) (Dulcan p.368)
epidemiology.heritability: 25-28% GWAS to 40-58% twin studies (DSM p.268, Dulcan p.370)
comorbidities: Tic disorders up to 30% (DSM p.271, Dulcan p.368)
epidemiology.prognosis: Chronic waxing-waning course; 40-60% persist into adulthood (Dulcan p.368, DSM p.267)

etiology.genetic: Polygenic; 10-fold increased risk in 1st-degree relatives for pediatric-onset (DSM p.268, Dulcan p.370)
etiology.neurobiology: CSTC loop dysfunction; OFC, ACC, Caudate, Thalamus; migration from ventral to dorsal habit circuit; 5-HT, Glutamate, DA (StahlNeuro p.539-540, p.575, Dulcan p.369)
etiology.environmental: Perinatal factors (maternal smoking, delivery complications, low birth weight), trauma, streptococcal infections (DSM p.268, Dulcan p.371-372)

first_line: CBT with Exposure and Response Prevention (ERP) for mild-moderate (Dulcan p.376, StahlNeuro p.576)
Combined CBT + SSRI (Sertraline, Fluoxetine, Fluvoxamine) for severe (CY-BOCS>=24) (Dulcan p.379-381, StahlKids p.129, p.201, p.227, p.415)
second_line: Augmentation with atypical antipsychotics (Aripiprazole, Risperidone) (Dulcan p.382, Synopsis ch.9)
key_side_effects: SSRI: GI distress, activation, insomnia, sexual dysfunction, suicidal ideation risk (StahlKids p.202, p.417)
Clomipramine: QTc prolongation, sedation, anticholinergic effects, seizure risk (StahlKids p.129-130)
treatment.monitoring: Baseline and titration ECG for Clomipramine (StahlKids p.129); CY-BOCS score, activation, and suicidality every 4-8 weeks (Dulcan p.374, p.379)

items: CY-BOCS clinician-administered gold standard scale (Dulcan p.374)
CY-BOCS II includes avoidance rating (Dulcan p.374)
COIS assesses child OCD functional impact (Dulcan p.375)
FAS-IR measures family accommodation (Dulcan p.373, p.375)
key_numbers: 0-40 total score range on CY-BOCS (Dulcan p.374)
35% score reduction defines clinical response (Dulcan p.374)

items: PANDAS: Post-streptococcal autoimmune basal ganglia inflammation (Dulcan p.369-370)
PANS: Acute onset OCD or ARFID with neuropsychiatric symptoms (Dulcan p.370)
Basal ganglia infarction, tumors, or Huntington disease (DSM p.292)
key_numbers: 2 distinct GABHS infections linked temporally to exacerbations for PANDAS (Dulcan p.370)
3-12 years age range for pre-pubertal PANDAS onset (Dulcan p.370)

items: With good/fair insight: recognizes OCD beliefs are likely false (DSM p.266)
With poor insight: thinks OCD beliefs are probably true (DSM p.266)
With absent insight/delusional beliefs: completely convinced beliefs are true (DSM p.266)
Absent insight does not require separate psychosis diagnosis if thoughts are OCD-restricted (DSM p.108, p.266)
5 items evaluate obsessions (time, interference, distress, resistance, control) (Dulcan p.374)
5 items evaluate compulsions (time, interference, distress, resistance, control) (Dulcan p.374)
Checklist covers contamination, harm, symmetry, taboo thoughts, and rituals (Dulcan p.374)

high_yield: Pediatric onset OCD has a 10-fold increase in 1st-degree relative risk vs 2-fold in adults (DSM p.268, Dulcan p.370)
Children with OCD and comorbid tics DO NOT respond to SSRI monotherapy; they require CBT or combined therapy (Dulcan p.368, p.381)
FDA approval ages: Sertraline (age 6+), Fluoxetine (age 7+), Fluvoxamine (age 8+), Clomipramine (age 10+) (StahlKids p.129, p.201, p.227, p.415)
Clomipramine requires mandatory ECG monitoring due to QTc prolongation and arrhythmia risk (StahlKids p.129-130, Dulcan p.380)
CSTC habit loops migrate from ventral (impulsive/VMPFC-accumbens) to dorsal (compulsive/OFC-caudate) (StahlNeuro p.539-540, p.575)
Absent insight specifier does not mean schizophrenia unless delusional content extends beyond OCD themes (DSM p.108, p.266)
